blocks.text: : Chemoprophylaxis options for special risk groups

The term chemoprophylaxis is used to describe the administration of an antimalarial drug or drug combination in such a way that blood levels are maintained above the inhibitory level of survival of the local strains of parasite for the whole of the period at risk and, in the case of travelers, for an appropriate period afterwards in order to kill emerging liver forms. The recommended medicines are atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline, and mefloquine.

: Malaria chemoprophylaxis in sickle cell disease
Sickle cell disease (SCD) is an inherited condition where the sickle cell gene responsible for the production of abnormal haemoglobin S is inherited from both parents.

runs.text: abnormal haemoglobin S is inherited from both parents.

blocks.text: In areas where malaria is common, SCD patients have low risk or malaria infection. However, when they do get malaria, it is associated with high risk of morbidity and mortality.

runs.text: In areas where malaria is common, SCD patients have low risk or malaria infection. However, when they do get malaria, it
is associated with high risk of morbidity and mortality.

blocks.text: It is recommended to give routine malaria prevention medicines (chemoprophylaxis) to individuals with SCD in areas where malaria is endemic. This helps to reduce SCD crises and all other related complications.

runs.text: It is recommended to give routine malaria prevention medicines (chemoprophylaxis) to individuals with SCD in areas where malaria is endemic. This helps to reduce SCD crises and all other related complications.

blocks.text: The recommended chemoprophylaxis in Tanzania is:
C: atovaquone + proguanil: daily administration according to body weight
C: dihydroartemisinin + piperaquine (FDC) (PO): monthly administration according to body weight
Due to available safe and effective pharmacological action every SCD patient who require protection must receive a suitable chemoprevention treatment.
